Developers can now install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7, just one week after the release of beta 6. Here are the details.

Apple Releases macOS 27 Beta 7

Last Monday, Apple ended a three-week beta hiatus by releasing macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6, which introduced redesigned traffic light window buttons. macOS 27 beta 6 no longer uses flat-design red, yellow, and green circles; instead, it adds a Liquid Glass-like (though really closer to Aqua) effect to the minimise, maximise, and close buttons.

Beyond that, macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 6 appears to have no other user-facing features or improvements, which may suggest Apple is using the final few betas to focus on bug fixes, performance, and security improvements ahead of launch.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a brand-new Siri app alongside an improved Siri AI. It also features a new AI-powered version of the Shortcuts app, allowing users to build shortcuts using natural language commands, and offers a prompt-based Safari extension builder.

Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a brand-new Golden Gate-themed wallpaper and screensaver, while reverting window and app corner-radius to a constant design. This reverses a change from macOS 26, which adjusted the corner radius according to the content of each window or app's menu bar.

The build number for macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 7 is 26A5421a. We're digging in now and will report back with what we find.

How to Install macOS 27 Golden Gate Beta

Here are the steps to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the 'i' icon next to Beta Updates
  • From the dropdown in the top-right corner, select macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta
  • Click Done

Have you spotted any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments.
